clue.text: Prepare to stop game for drink

definitions.meaning: a referee readies the whistle at the lips before blowing to halt play
to have a drink, colloquially to moisten the throat

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to break off a match and go for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a drink, and literally describes moistening a referee's whistle before blowing it.

clue.text: Speak of that such as iron spirit

indicators.note: speaking the word out loud gives a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: iron is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A remark about iron having a certain spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is courage or spirit, the quality of facing difficulty with resolve.

clue.text: Skin application brings agony, piercing skin blemish

indicators.note: one piece goes through and sits inside the other, as a stud pierces flesh

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin
agony is extreme pain

explanation.surface: A cream for the skin hurts when it gets into a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is decorative paint applied to the face and body, hence an application to the skin.

clue.text: Film Keith suggested?

parts.note: the name sits inside a stretch of the title, so part of the title points to the name

explanation.surface: A movie that Keith recommended.
explanation.walkthrough: KEITH runs through liKE IT Hot, so SOME of LIKE IT HOT suggests Keith.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Like It Hot is the 1959 Billy Wilder comedy film starring Marilyn Monroe.

clue.text: Biased as a brunette, you might say?

definitions.meaning: partial, not treating all sides equally
someone with dark hair is jokingly described as not light-haired

explanation.surface: A prejudiced remark about a dark-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair is a synonym of biased, and playfully means not fair-haired, as a brunette is.

clue.text: Isolation thus illuminated due to switch

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
lit means lighted up

indicators.note: to switch the letters is to change their order around

explanation.surface: Being cut off because the lights were switched on, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' rearranges DUE into UDE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitude is the state of being alone, a synonym for isolation.

clue.text: Lift to reveal cracks

indicators.note: the phrase is broken apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Raising something to expose fissures.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevator is the American word for a lift carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Be a snitch, as a schoolboy should be?

definitions.meaning: to tell tales on someone to authority
a pupil is expected to be inside his class group, a form in British schools

explanation.surface: Telling tales, as a good schoolboy supposedly should.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform is to give incriminating information; read as two words it means placed within a school class.

clue.text: Try nice matches to develop team

indicators.note: the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An attempt to bring on good fixtures for a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester City is an English Premier League football club, so an example of a team.

clue.text: No digital coordinator when surfing, better off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are spoiled or out of order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy is better off not surfing.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfingers is a clumsy person who drops things, lacking coordination of the fingers, or digits.

clue.text: Books collected by pensioner, readily available

indicators.note: one piece is gathered up inside the other

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A retired person picks up some books that were easy to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap, like beer from a barrel, is ready to be drawn whenever needed.

clue.text: Doctor cautioned for drilling

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician warned someone about dental work.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilling in the sense of repeated training or instruction is a kind of schooling.

clue.text: Item about holding anger back for those given honourable discharge

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around
the word is read from right to left

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: An object concerned with restraining rage among people released from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ITEM into EMIT; 'back' turns IRE into ERI, which EMIT holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors who keep their title as an honour, so retired with distinction.

clue.text: As a result of being finished

explanation.surface: Being done as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Through can mean by reason of, as in succeeding through effort, and also completed, as in being done with something.

clue.text: Take strides to appear the dominant partner?

definitions.meaning: strides is British slang for trousers, so to put them on
to be seen as the one in charge in a couple

explanation.surface: Walking boldly to look like the boss in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be the dominant partner in a relationship, and literally means to have trousers on.

clue.text: An order from the dessert trolley?

definitions.text: An order from the dessert trolley?

parts.words: An order from the dessert trolley?
parts.note: a request for a sweet baked dish, and also a phrase meaning perfect tidiness

explanation.surface: Asking for a pudding in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat phrase for perfect tidiness, and also a fruit dessert one might order.

clue.text: Ebullient party anything but down within Tate Modern

parts.note: ebullient means high-spirited, which is up in the informal sense

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
in a down entry, going the opposite way to down means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A lively gathering in a London art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anything but down' turns DO into OD, which goes 'within' TATE. The Tate Modern is a London art gallery, which disguises 'Modern' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date means current or contemporary, a synonym of modern.

clue.text: Surgical insertion Mudd's twentieth strategy?

parts.note: Mudd is the setter, so Mudd is becomes I am, shortened
a plan is a strategy
T is the twentieth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The setter's twentieth scheme involves a medical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: An implant is something inserted into the body by surgery, such as a pacemaker.

clue.text: Girl given drink before six turn up

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: the number written as a word

explanation.surface: A young woman gets a beer ahead of six people arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexis is a given name for a girl.

clue.text: Passionate in the past, perhaps

parts.note: the past is an example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone who used to be passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means full of strong feeling, a synonym for passionate.

clue.text: Common girl, leader of ladettes

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A vulgar young woman heads a gang of rowdy girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladettes are boisterous young women in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means ordinary, a sense of common.

clue.text: The elementary particle needs good familiar air

parts.note: a meson is a subatomic particle

explanation.surface: A physics particle needs a good, well-known atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is a tune identified with a show or person, so a recognisable air or melody.

clue.text: Finland or Iceland keeping order in Greece

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Two Nordic countries maintaining law and order in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, alongside Ionic and Corinthian.

clue.text: Evoke the ultimate in allegiance within the law

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Calling up the final word in loyalty within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response, which is to evoke it.

clue.text: Expert given some land to extend

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A specialist is handed some territory to enlarge.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw out, a synonym of extend.
